title: Pharaoh's dreams (Genesis 41)
hookLine: seven fat cows, seven thin ones, and a plan to store grain

cards: Two full years after the butler forgot, Pharaoh has a nightmare. He's standing by the Nile, and seven cows come up out of the river, sleek and fat, and graze in the reeds.
Then seven more come up, thin and ugly, and eat the seven fat cows. And they're still just as thin.
Pharaoh wakes, falls back asleep, and dreams again: seven full ears of grain on one stalk, swallowed by seven thin, scorched ones. All the wise men of Egypt are called. Nobody can explain it.
And suddenly the butler, standing right there, remembers something.

teach.b: They rush Joseph out of the dungeon. He shaves and changes his clothes, another change of garment in this story, and stands before Pharaoh. I hear you can interpret dreams, says the king.
Joseph's first words: "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace." Not me. God.
The two dreams are one, he explains. Seven good years are coming, years of plenty across Egypt.

teach.h: SEVEN OF PLENTY, SEVEN OF FAMINE.
teach.b: Then seven years of famine, so heavy that the plenty will be forgotten. The dream came twice because it's certain, and soon. But Joseph doesn't stop at explaining.

teach.h: STORE A FIFTH IN THE GOOD YEARS.
teach.b: He gives Pharaoh a plan: find a wise man, collect a fifth of the harvest in the good years, store the grain in the cities, and when the famine comes, the country won't perish.
Pharaoh looks around: who could be wiser than the man who just said this?
Joseph goes from the prison to the palace, second only to Pharaoh. He's thirty years old. He was seventeen in the pit.
He gets a ring, fine linen, a gold chain, an Egyptian name, and a wife. His two sons' names tell you what's inside him. Manasseh: God made me forget my hardship and my father's house.
Ephraim: God made me fruitful in the land of my suffering.
In the good years, Joseph stores grain beyond counting. When the barns are full, a famine is easy to forget. That's exactly when he gets ready.

how: Jews read this chapter in the weekly Torah portion Miketz, which the calendar often places during Hanukkah.

o: a sign that Pharaoh's reign would end soon
a curse on the Nile sent by Egypt's gods
a warning: seven years of plenty, then famine

games.q: what's inside the dreams — tap the pairs.
p: God made me forget my hardship

s: Joseph said he had a gift for reading dreams
"It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace."
Joseph was thirty when he stood before Pharaoh
he was seventeen when his brothers sold him. thirteen years passed.
he also gave Pharaoh a plan: store a fifth of the harvest in the good years.

games.q: you're Joseph. you've just explained Pharaoh's dreams. famine is coming. what do you do next?
o: bow and wait to be sent back to prison.
propose a plan to store grain.
ask to be sent home to your father.
games.why: he proposes a plan: a wise man, a fifth of the harvest, grain stored in the cities. Pharaoh chooses him to run it.

practice: Think about what's plentiful in your life right now, money, time, energy, friends, patience, and pick one.
Then picture a leaner season that might come, and one small thing you could store up for it now: a few dollars, a phone call to keep a friendship warm, a good night's sleep.

wordCard.voice: Pharaoh's dreams. Seven fat cows and seven thin: seven years of plenty, seven of famine, and a plan to store grain in the good years.

orig.note: Hebrew: plenty, being full. its opposite in the dream is ra'av, famine.

carryVoice: Your line: store in the good years. Reading the dream was the easy part. Seventy days now: ten whole weeks.

sources.q: It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
